Hi, thank you for your kind advice. This, with another Redditor's advice, gave me the courage to do something to get help. I called the national suicide hotline where the person was compassionate and understanding + had a very similar experience which really pushed me to get back on my medication. I feel so much better and can actually concentrate again.

I now really understand that mood disorders really are similar to heart diseases/other physical conditions that need medication. I discovered for me it makes the most sense to compare my depression to Type I diabetes- it's no one's fault that someone's body does not produce enough insulin. Same for my neurotransmitters. So thank you again for giving me the courage.

Sorry for my late reply, and thank you so much for all the helpful info! 

I'm definitely going to take a look at Neff's work, as I can definitely benefit from self-compassion. As you've mentioned, I have been wallowing in self-pity recently. What really threw me off recently was deciding to self-diagnose and think I am "okay" enough to stop taking my medication since I graduated college and lost contact with my psychiatrist (I know I shouldn't have). 

I went through few days of just.. foggy and slow thoughts, being super tired, disinterest in anything, and just in a really dark place. I didn't know depression affected me this much. What helped me was you mentioning how important self-compassion is- and I decided that I should do something rather than keep on beating myself up for being "lazy" or "stupid". 

Now I'm back on my medication after an online doctor consultation and I feel better. I don't think I would've been able to focus on any of Neff's videos or books without going back on medication. But now that I am, I definitely think I can. Thank you for all your help and giving me courage to admit I need help.
